target.title: fix(web): avoid exact-limit fetch truncation warnings
target.body:
﻿Closes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running web_fetch could see a response reported as truncated when the streamed response body was exactly maxResponseBytes bytes, even though no bytes were omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

eadResponseText now treats truncation as proven only when a chunk exceeds the remaining byte budget. Reaching the byte budget exactly no longer flips the truncation flag by itself, so exact-limit responses can complete normally while true overflow still cancels the reader.

## User Impact

Users no longer get misleading Response body truncated after ... bytes. warnings for complete responses that happen to land exactly on the byte cap. Oversized responses are still bounded and marked truncated.

## Evidence

- Current-main source check: src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts previously set 	runcated = true when  ytesRead >= maxBytes; src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts surfaces that flag as a user-visible warning.
- Focused regression: 
ode scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts passed in the temporary validation worktree with the same two-file patch, 1 file / 12 tests.
- Whitespace check: git diff --check passed in the final PR worktree.
- Duplicate search: no open issue or PR found for web_fetch truncated maxBytes exact limit or eadResponseText truncated maxBytes.

Validation notes: Testbox-through-Crabbox was unavailable in this environment because no usable crabbox binary was on PATH and the wrapper failed its binary sanity check. The mandatory autoreview helper also did not produce a review result: first run hit Windows UTF-8 config decoding, and the UTF-8 retry reached Codex but failed with an invalid local OpenAI API key (401). The diff was kept to the two touched files above.
